subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on Food Science, then mark my answer against the Edexcel spec.
promptWeak: Explain Food Science for GCSE Edexcel Food Preparation & Nutrition simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Which is NOT a reason for cooking food?
options: To reduce all its nutritional value
To make it easier to digest
To make it safer to eat
questions.explain: Food is cooked to make it safe, more palatable, easier to digest and to give variety. Reducing nutritional value is a possible side effect, not a reason to cook.

questions.q: Heat passing through a metal pan into food sitting on the base is an example of:
questions.explain: Conduction is the transfer of heat through direct contact in a solid, such as a metal pan base heating the food touching it.

questions.q: Which cooking method relies mainly on convection currents?
options: Boiling vegetables in a pan of water
Frying an egg in a pan
questions.explain: In boiling, hot water rises and cooler water sinks, setting up convection currents that circulate heat. Grilling and toasting use radiation; frying uses conduction.

questions.q: Grilling and toasting cook food mainly by which method of heat transfer?
questions.explain: Grilling and toasting use radiation: infra-red waves travel from the hot element to the surface of the food without heating the air in between.

questions.q: When an egg white turns from clear liquid to a firm white solid on heating, this is called:
questions.explain: Heat denatures the egg proteins, unravelling them, and they then coagulate (set) into a solid mass. This is why eggs set when cooked.

questions.q: Which of these can cause a protein to denature WITHOUT using heat?
options: Adding an acid such as lemon juice
questions.explain: Proteins can be denatured by heat, acid (e.g. lemon juice or vinegar), or mechanical action such as whisking. Denaturing changes their structure permanently.

questions.q: Gluten is formed when which proteins in wheat flour are mixed with water and kneaded?
questions.explain: The wheat proteins gliadin and glutenin combine with water during kneading to form gluten, a stretchy network that gives bread dough its structure and elasticity.

questions.q: Why is strong (bread) flour used to make bread rather than plain flour?
options: It has a higher protein content, forming more gluten
questions.explain: Strong flour has a higher protein content, so it forms more gluten. The strong, stretchy gluten network traps gas and gives bread a good rise and chewy structure.

questions.q: During gelatinisation, starch granules in a sauce:
options: Swell, absorb liquid and thicken the mixture
Break down into sugars by dry heat
Trap air to make it light
questions.explain: When a starch-liquid mixture is heated (around 55-85 degrees C), the starch granules absorb liquid, swell and burst, releasing starch that thickens the sauce.

questions.q: A student's white sauce is lumpy. What is the best way to prevent this?
options: Add all the flour at the end
Use cold milk only and do not heat it
Stir continuously while heating and add liquid gradually
Boil it as fast as possible with no stirring
questions.explain: Stirring continuously and adding liquid gradually keeps the starch granules separated so they gelatinise evenly, giving a smooth sauce rather than lumps.

questions.q: The browning of the crust of bread or toast under dry heat is caused by:
questions.explain: Dextrinisation is the browning of starch by dry heat, breaking starch into dextrins. It gives toast, bread crusts and pastry their golden-brown colour.

questions.q: Sugar heated in a pan turns golden brown and develops a rich flavour. This is:
questions.explain: Caramelisation is the browning of sugar when heated, producing colour and a characteristic sweet, nutty flavour, as when making caramel or the top of a creme brulee.

questions.q: Rubbing fat into flour to coat the flour particles and give a crumbly texture is an example of:
questions.explain: Shortening is when fat coats flour particles, preventing gluten formation and giving a short, crumbly texture as in shortcrust pastry and biscuits.

questions.q: Creaming butter and sugar together traps air. This function is called:
questions.explain: Aeration is the trapping of air into a mixture, for example by creaming fat and sugar or whisking eggs, which helps cakes and sponges rise and become light.

questions.q: Which ingredient acts as an emulsifier to stop oil and vinegar separating in mayonnaise?
questions.explain: Egg yolk contains lecithin, a natural emulsifier that holds oil and water-based liquids together in a stable emulsion, as in mayonnaise.

questions.q: An emulsion is a mixture of:
options: Two liquids that would normally separate, such as oil and water
questions.explain: An emulsion is a mixture of two liquids that normally do not mix (oil and water), held together by an emulsifier so they stay combined.

questions.q: Which gas do most raising agents produce to make baked goods rise?
questions.explain: Chemical raising agents (baking powder, bicarbonate of soda) and yeast produce carbon dioxide, which expands on heating and makes mixtures rise.

questions.q: Which is a biological raising agent used in bread?
questions.explain: Yeast is a biological raising agent: it ferments sugars and produces carbon dioxide, making bread dough rise. Baking powder is chemical; steam is a mechanical/physical raising agent.

questions.q: In a well-whisked sponge with no baking powder, what mainly makes it rise?
options: Air trapped by whisking, which expands on heating
questions.explain: A whisked sponge rises because whisking traps air (a mechanical raising agent); the trapped air and steam expand on heating to lift the mixture.

questions.q: A cut apple turns brown. Which action best slows this enzymic browning?
options: Leaving it exposed to warm air
Cutting it into larger pieces only
Coating the surface with lemon juice
questions.explain: Enzymic browning is caused by enzymes reacting with oxygen. The acid (vitamin C) in lemon juice slows the enzyme, so coating cut fruit in lemon juice reduces browning.
